name: Silk weaving in Yangshao-culture Henan
summary: People of the Yangshao culture in Henan wove silk cloth about 5,500 to 5,300 years ago and wrapped their dead in it, the earliest silk fabrics yet identified.
description: Carbonised fabric from an urn coffin at the Wanggou site in Henan, among Neolithic Yangshao-culture ruins, was confirmed as silk by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay developed at the China National Silk Museum. The fabrics wrapped the bodies of the dead, were woven of fine yarns, and one was dyed before weaving, which the excavators take to show that silk making had matured by then. The same fabrics are reported from the Qingtai site, and the excavators infer from these finds and from bone carvings of silkworms at Shuanghuaishu that silkworms were being raised more than 5,000 years ago; that inference comes from a press report, and no peer-reviewed paper was checked.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited page: silk making stayed within China for millennia and then spread across Asia to the Mediterranean, but as a costly cloth for a minority, so reach is 2; it gave a new fibre and a new industry (depth 2), and reeling, patterned-loom weaving and the long-distance silk trade grew from it (generativity 2).

date.label: c. 3550 to 3350 BCE (5,500 to 5,300 years ago)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Carbonised silk fabrics from an urn coffin at Wanggou in Henan are dated to between 5,300 and 5,500 years ago, about 3550 to 3350 BCE.

evidence.supports: The silk fabrics at the Wanggou date back between 5,300 and 5,500 years.
evidence.locator: Paragraph on dating, after the ELISA identification

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Find the peer-reviewed publication of the Wanggou silk identification and dating; this card relies on the Xinhua press report.
The place is Henan province as a whole because the source gives no coordinates for Wanggou; refine to the site.

Qianshanyang (Liangzhu culture, 4,200 to 4,400 years ago per Xinhua) is a later benchmark that may need its own record; the Jiahu silk-protein residues (Gong et al. 2016) were not checked and would bear on the first-known claim.
The silkworm bone carvings at Shuanghuaishu are reported by Xinhua without a date, and nothing here dates the domestication of the silkworm.

research.note: Xinhua reports, on the word of the excavating institute and the China National Silk Museum, that these are the world's earliest silk fabrics found; the claim is about woven fabric, rests on a press report, and earlier indirect traces of silk claimed elsewhere in China were not checked.
